summary.headline: GHCL Q4 FY26 revenue flat YoY at INR 808 crore; EBITDA margin rose to 23.9% as volumes (~11%) offset pricing (~-10%).
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 808 crore, flat YoY and up from INR 773 crore in Q3, with sequential gains attributed to better domestic volumes and realisations. EBITDA was INR 194 crore (23.9% margin) versus INR 175 crore in Q3 and INR 244 crore a year ago; PAT was INR 120 crore. FY26 revenue was INR 3,144 crore and PAT INR 479 crore (15.2% net margin), with INR 415 crore returned via dividend and buyback. Management said global soda ash oversupply persists but import curbs from higher freight and a weaker rupee have firmed domestic prices from March. Bromine and vacuum salt projects are nearing full commissioning in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Soda ash (core)
segments.commentary: Management cited ~11% volume growth against ~10% price decline YoY. Domestic prices firmed from March as imports fell on freight costs and a weaker rupee; costs were passed through to customers.

segments.name: Sodium bicarbonate
segments.commentary: Volumes grew in FY26 with utilisation around 80-85%; management expects slightly better demand in FY27.

segments.name: Bromine and vacuum salt (new)
segments.commentary: First leg commissioned; full commissioning expected Q1 FY27. Guided FY27 revenue ~INR 120 crore (peak ~INR 170 crore) at 40-45% EBITDA margin. Pricing for bromine described as significantly higher than planned.

guidance_outlook: Bromine and vacuum salt projects expected to be fully commissioned in Q1 FY27; about INR 300 crore of CWIP to capitalise on commissioning.
FY27 incremental revenue from bromine and vacuum salt guided at ~INR 120 crore, peak ~INR 170 crore, EBITDA margin 40-45%; utilisation to ramp through the year to full capacity by year-end.
EBITDA margin outlook described as roughly neutral to slightly positive, with management declining to forecast beyond the near term.
Greenfield soda ash project: funded by mix of internal accruals and debt; debt-equity to stay below 1; construction timeline not yet fixed pending land acquisition and conversion.
Anti-dumping duty recommendation is with the finance ministry with no decision; a safeguard (quantitative restriction) application is under investigation, taking some months.
capex_capacity: Bromine and vacuum salt: first leg commissioned; full commissioning expected Q1 FY27 (May-June ramp).
Greenfield soda ash: construction start not yet fixed; land acquisition and conversion ongoing; project expected to take 2.5-3 years once started, with capex weighted to later years.
Sodium bicarbonate capacity doubled earlier; utilisation ~80-85%.
Soda ash capacity mix: roughly 50-55% dense (glass) and ~50% light (detergent); management aims to raise dense share from existing assets without major capex.
Pipeline project at existing facility also in CWIP, expected to be commissioned in FY27.
demand_pricing: Indian soda ash demand grew ~6% last year; management expects growth to continue in FY27, led by solar glass. Solar glass ramp-up adds several thousand tonnes per month of dense soda ash demand.
Imports into India have fallen in the last quarter due to higher freight and supply-chain delays; domestic inventory has eased and prices firmed, with March showing some increase.

Global oversupply persists; China demand recovery slower than expected; Inner Mongolia added ~2.5-3 million tonnes in the last year, taking the province to ~7 million tonnes; a US facility of ~1.3 million tonnes is mothballed.

Cost pressures: coal/energy index rose from ~$120 to ~$136 (volatile); limestone freight from the Middle East increased; packaging and other costs also rose. Management says cost increases have been passed through.
Raw material inventory covers about four to five months, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the flat top line was volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes rose ~11% while pricing fell ~10% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How are funding and capital return balanced for the greenfield soda ash project?
qa_highlights.answer: Funding will be a mix of internal accruals and debt, with debt-equity kept below 1. Cash of about INR 1,000 crore is on the balance sheet; management said shareholder payouts are a conscious choice and the distribution pattern may change as the project progresses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and margin from bromine and vacuum salt in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly INR 120 crore in FY27 (full-year run-rate about INR 160 crore), with 40-45% EBITDA margin; peak around INR 170 crore once fully ramped.

qa_highlights.question: How much CWIP will be capitalised and what is the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 300 crore of the INR 450 crore CWIP will be capitalised once the bromine and vacuum salt projects are commissioned in Q1; a pipeline project at the existing facility is also in CWIP and is expected to be commissioned this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are roughly neutral to slightly positive given cost increases offset by realisation gains, and declined to forecast beyond the near term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of anti-dumping and safeguard duties?
qa_highlights.answer: Anti-dumping recommendation has gone to the finance ministry with no decision; a fresh safeguard quantitative-restriction application is under investigation and will take some months.

risks_watch: Soda ash pricing remains exposed to global oversupply and Chinese synthetic producers; price recovery depends on geopolitics and import curbs.
Energy and freight cost inflation (coal, limestone, shipping) linked to the US-Iran conflict; pass-through success needs monitoring in Q1 FY27 margins.
Timing of bromine and vacuum salt full commissioning in Q1 FY27 and the ramp to INR 120 crore FY27 revenue.
Greenfield soda ash project: no construction start date; land acquisition delays and debt-funded capex ahead.
Anti-dumping decision pending with the finance ministry; safeguard duty application under investigation.
Net payout of ~87% of FY26 PAT could limit cash retention if the greenfield project scales up.
summary.management_tone: Confident on cost control and the domestic demand outlook, but cautious and noncommittal on pricing, margins, and project timelines, repeatedly citing geopolitical volatility. Management was evasive on the greenfield construction start and on margin guidance beyond the near term.
key_quotes: And we believe our low-cost foundation positions us among the first to benefit as and when pricing recovers.
The Indian market appears to be approaching an inflection point.
FY27 makes the beginning of a new earning layer for GHCL.
